name: Paracetamol (Acetaminophen)
purpose: Relieves mild-to-moderate pain and reduces fever.
howToTake: Usually taken after food to reduce the chance of an upset stomach. Follow the exact dose, frequency, and duration your doctor wrote on the prescription — don't self-adjust.
goodFoods: Plain rice or khichdi if appetite is low
avoidDrinks: Alcohol — increases liver strain when combined with paracetamol
lifestyleTips: Rest and stay hydrated
Use a light sponge bath if fever is high
Monitor temperature every few hours
commonSideEffects: Rare at normal doses; nausea in some people

name: Ibuprofen
howToTake: Take with food or milk — never on an empty stomach, since it can irritate the stomach lining.
goodFoods: Milk, curd, or a light meal before/with the dose
avoidFoods: Very spicy or acidic foods on an empty stomach
avoidDrinks: Excess caffeine if you have acidity issues
lifestyleTips: Avoid taking on an empty stomach
Don't combine with other NSAIDs unless your doctor says so

name: Amoxicillin
purpose: Treats bacterial infections (throat, ear, chest, urinary tract, etc.).
howToTake: Complete the FULL course even if you feel better early — stopping early can let bacteria survive and become resistant.
goodFoods: Probiotic foods like curd/yogurt to support gut bacteria
avoidFoods: Nothing specific, but avoid very sugary foods that can worsen an existing infection
avoidDrinks: Alcohol during the course, if advised by your doctor
lifestyleTips: Take doses at evenly spaced times
Stay hydrated to help your body recover
commonSideEffects: Skin rash (report this to your doctor)
whenToSeekHelp: Hives, facial swelling, or trouble breathing (possible allergic reaction)

name: Azithromycin
purpose: Treats bacterial infections, often respiratory or skin infections.
howToTake: Usually taken once a day, at the same time, for the number of days prescribed — complete the full course.
avoidFoods: Very heavy or oily meals right before the dose
avoidDrinks: Antacids close to dosing time — they can reduce absorption
lifestyleTips: Space out antacids and this medicine by a couple of hours if you take both

name: Metformin
purpose: Helps manage blood sugar levels in type 2 diabetes.
howToTake: Typically taken with or right after meals to reduce stomach discomfort.
avoidDrinks: Alcohol — raises the risk of low blood sugar and other complications
lifestyleTips: Regular light exercise (like a daily walk)
Consistent meal timings
Monitor blood sugar as your doctor advises
whenToSeekHelp: Unusual muscle pain with weakness/breathing trouble
Signs of very low blood sugar (shaking, confusion, sweating)

name: Amlodipine
purpose: Relaxes blood vessels to lower blood pressure.
howToTake: Usually taken once daily, at the same time each day, with or without food.
goodFoods: Potassium-rich foods like bananas and leafy greens (unless your doctor says otherwise)
avoidDrinks: Grapefruit juice — can interact with this medicine
lifestyleTips: Reduce salt intake
Regular light cardio if your doctor approves
Track blood pressure periodically

name: Omeprazole
purpose: Reduces stomach acid — used for acidity, ulcers, and reflux (GERD).
howToTake: Best taken on an empty stomach, about 30–60 minutes before a meal, usually in the morning.
avoidFoods: Citrus fruits and tomatoes if they trigger reflux
avoidDrinks: Coffee, carbonated drinks, and alcohol — all can worsen acidity
lifestyleTips: Don't lie down immediately after eating
Avoid late-night heavy meals
Elevate the head of the bed if reflux is worse at night

name: Cetirizine
purpose: Relieves allergy symptoms like sneezing, itching, and runny nose.
howToTake: Usually taken once daily, often at night since it can cause mild drowsiness in some people.
lifestyleTips: Avoid driving/operating machinery if you feel drowsy
Identify and reduce exposure to your allergy triggers

name: Vitamin D3
purpose: Supports bone health, calcium absorption, and immune function.
howToTake: Best absorbed when taken with a meal that contains some fat.
avoidFoods: No major restrictions — pair with a normal meal for better absorption
lifestyleTips: Get 15–20 minutes of morning sunlight when possible
Pair with light weight-bearing exercise for bone health
whenToSeekHelp: Symptoms of excess vitamin D (nausea, weakness) — very rare, but report to your doctor

name: Iron (Ferrous Sulfate)
howToTake: Best absorbed on an empty stomach, but can be taken with light food if it causes nausea.
goodFoods: Vitamin C-rich foods (citrus, amla, tomato) to boost absorption
avoidFoods: Dairy products close to dosing time — calcium can reduce iron absorption
avoidDrinks: Tea and coffee within an hour of the dose — tannins reduce iron absorption
lifestyleTips: Take with a vitamin-C source like lemon or orange for better absorption
Space out tea/coffee from dosing time
whenToSeekHelp: Black stools with dizziness (unrelated to iron colouring)
